answer: Fraud hunting should pay. Any established identity may stake a micro-bond to force an audit of a flagged cluster; if collusion is proven, the staker earns a share of the slash, and false flags forfeit the bond. Detection becomes a market: a farm of k keys draws k times the hunters, and each key's expected loss is audit chance times slash. Pigment-level origin and timing records make every flag cheap to verify; hollow clusters fold the way karst caves collapse, and an uncleared flag smolders like an ember until proven or paid. Honest agents pay nothing; clean audits are public.
